prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the downward-sloping outdoor scene on a wooden boardwalk (~1.2–2.0 m below eye level) flanked by recessed vegetation, with the camera wearer's hands and blue poncho in the brightest foreground (~0.3–0.5 m) at the bottom. A person in a blue jacket and yellow vest stands directly in front and slightly left (~0.5–0.8 m away, head cropped above the frame) facing the camera wearer, while a second person in a dark poncho retreats up the boardwalk from ~0.8 m in frame 1 to ~1.8 m in frame 2 (occluded behind the first person in frames 3–4) and a third person in a yellow poncho stands ~0.8–1.2 m to the right (~0.7 m from the first person, partially out of view at the right edge). Across frames 1 to 5, the camera wearer's gloved left hand and bare right hand reach forward to meet the first person's outstretched right hand within arm's reach (~0.4–0.5 m) to pass a small snack bar, before the camera wearer's left hand drops back slightly in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradients clearly separate the overlapping hands and arms from the boardwalk and vegetation beneath them and show the relative elevation of the raised hands above the ground plane. However, the map is unreliable in scale consistency across frames—such as the first person's shoulder abruptly saturating to bright white in frame 2 while appearing mid-grey in frame 3 despite minimal distance change—and it merges the snack bar into the surrounding hand surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels portions of the people on the boardwalk against an unlabelled black background, showing the camera wearer's hands and poncho at the bottom (~0.3–0.5 m), the inward-facing person in the blue jacket in the upper-left/centre (~0.5–0.8 m), the retreating person's legs above them in frames 2 and 5 (~1.5–2.0 m), and the third person on the right edge (~0.8–1.2 m away and ~0.7 m from the central person). While the map outlines the spatial convergence of the camera wearer's hands and the first person's extended right arm within arm's reach (~0.4–0.5 m) in frames 3–5, all heads remain cropped above the top edge so gaze direction cannot be determined. It makes the distant, dark legs of the retreating person at the top of frames 2 and 5 easier to isolate as distinct human instances than in the dark RGB shadows. However, the map is highly unreliable for instance separation and class accuracy: it omits the boardwalk, vegetation, and handheld snack bar entirely, misses the camera wearer's hands in frame 2, splits the blue-jacketed person into separate masks for their jacket and yellow vest in frame 2, and merges the camera wearer's left arm and the first person's body into a single cyan mask across an arbitrary horizontal seam in frames 3 and 4. Furthermore, in frame 5 it falsely classifies the camera wearer's dark-gloved left hand as a 'bird' while fragmenting the overlapping arms and right-side person into inconsistent mask pieces.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only isolated 2D hand skeletons in magenta on a completely black background, omitting all yellow body skeletons, scene layout, background objects, and head/torso orientations across all 5 frames. In frames 1 to 3, it detects only the extended right hand of the blue-jacketed person located in front and to the left of the camera wearer (~0.4–0.6 m away, within arm's reach), showing the open palm facing upward and inward as it lowers slightly toward the bottom-centre to meet the camera wearer's hands. In frame 4, it detects both the first person's open right hand and the camera wearer's right hand (~0.4 m away, touching at the centre-right) as the snack bar is transferred, before failing to detect any hands at all in frame 5 even though both remain clearly visible in the RGB image. Compared to RGB alone, the magenta keypoints explicitly articulate the five finger joints and palm orientation of the extended hand in frames 1–2 and the opposing thumb-and-finger grasp of the camera wearer's right hand in frame 4. However, the map is severely incomplete because heavy top-down foreshortening, cropped heads and torsos, and mutual occlusion by the dark glove and snack bar cause it to miss all three surrounding bodies, the camera wearer's gloved left hand in every frame, and the camera wearer's right hand in frames 1–3 and 5.
